newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Rating Agency Malaysia says debt ratings up in Apr.
newsitem.headline: Rating Agency Malaysia says debt ratings up in Apr.

text.p: The Rating Agency Malaysia Bhd (RAM) said it rated 10 bond issues in April worth 5.19 billion ringgit, against three totalling 1.16 billion ringgit in March.

But, the number of long-term bond issues that went to the market dropped to three totalling 940 million ringgit against four issues amounting to 1.63 billion ringgit in March, RAM said in its monthly report on the Malaysian debt market.

The three issues in April were ACP Industries' five-year Islamic debt securities for 100 million ringgit and Renong Bhd's 1.75 percent, five-year redeemable secured bonds for 390 million ringgit, and five-year zero-coupon bank guaranteed bonds for 450 million ringgit.
Among the issues rated in April, two were short-term and eight were long-term, RAM said.
In the first four months of the year, RAM has rated issues amounting to 7.8 billion ringgit, up over 100 percent from the corresponding period in 1996, it said.
However, the secondary over the counter (OTC) market remained inactive in April on fears that Bank Negara may step into the market to mop up liquidity, RAM said.
"Meanwhile, the market for listed bonds recorded stronger activities with the monthly volume traded rising from 7,017 lots to 10,504 lots in April," the report said.
